item.title: NAMING OF UGANDA'S CRUDE OIL
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: In a historic gathering along the southeastern shores of Lake Albert, on 2nd September, 2026. item.content:encoded:
President Museveni Officiates Naming of Uganda’s Crude Oil as Commercial Production Approaches

KIKUUBE DISTRICT — In a historic gathering along the southeastern shores of Lake Albert, on 2nd September, 2026. President Yoweri Museveni officiated the unveiling and ceremonial naming of Uganda’s crude oil. The landmark event, hosted at the Kingfisher Development Area, brings the country a step closer to commercial petroleum extraction.

The project naming convention bridges Uganda's natural ecosystem with its national heritage. The flagship Tilenga project operated by TotalEnergies across the Buliisa and Nwoya districts—blends the Acholi word "Til" and the Runyoro/Rutooro word "Engabi", both referencing the native Uganda Kob and Bushbuck antelopes. Meanwhile, the Kingfisher field in Kikuube District, managed by CNOOC Uganda Limited, draws its title from the agile, fish-eating bird native to the Lake Albert basin.

Uganda’s petroleum reserves, estimated at 6.5 billion barrels in place with up to 1.7 billion recoverable barrels, present unique technical properties. Classified as medium-sweet crude due to its low sulfur content, the oil is exceptionally waxy, solidifying at room temperatures. To transport it from the Albertine Graben to the Tanzanian port of Tanga, developers are constructing the 1,443-kilometer East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP), set to become the world’s longest electrically heat-traced pipeline.

The government and joint-venture partners maintain that overall infrastructure including the Central Processing Facilities (CPFs) and well pads remains on track to achieve first commercial oil. Once fully operational, the joint developments at Tilenga and Kingfisher are projected to reach a peak extraction capacity of approximately 230,000 barrels per day.

item.title: Academic Day & Club Exhibitions — July 11, 2026
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: Join us for our annual Academic Day and Club Exhibitions. Pupils will showcase their academic progress and club achievements. All parents and guardians are warmly invited.
item.content:encoded:
Bright Sparks Junior School warmly invites all parents, guardians, and friends to our annual Academic Day & Club Exhibitions on Saturday, July 11, 2026.

This is one of the most celebrated events in our school calendar. Pupils from all classes will display their academic work, creative projects, and the achievements of their co-curricular clubs including:

  • Music — Piano & Guitar performances
  • Cookery & Baking — tasting display
  • Chess & Checkers — live demonstrations
  • Ballet & Modelling — performance showcase
  • Swimming — certificate presentations

Academic progress reports and class performance highlights will also be shared with parents during the event.

Entry is free. Refreshments will be available. We look forward to seeing you!

item.title: Colour Day — Kindergarten Section (June 12)
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: Kindergarten pupils and their families are invited to celebrate Colour Day on June 12, 2026. Children are encouraged to dress in their favourite colours.
item.content:encoded:
Our Kindergarten section will celebrate Colour Day on Friday, June 12, 2026 — a vibrant, fun-filled day for our youngest learners and their families.

Children are encouraged to come dressed in their favourite colour or a mix of bright colours. The day will include themed activities, games, singing, and a special surprise for each class.

Parents and guardians are warmly welcome to join us for part of the celebration. More details on timings will be shared via the class WhatsApp groups and school notice board.

item.title: Eid Al Adhuha — School Closed May 27
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: In observance of Eid Al Adhuha, there will be no classes on Wednesday, May 27, 2026. We wish all our Muslim families a blessed celebration.
item.content:encoded:
In observance of Eid Al Adhuha — the Day of Sacrifice commemorating the faith demonstrated by Prophet Ibrahim — there will be no classes on Wednesday, May 27, 2026.

We wish all our Muslim families, staff, and pupils a blessed and joyful celebration. School resumes on Thursday, May 28 (Reporting Day for Term II).

item.title: Eid Al Adhuha
item.dc:creator: BrightSpark
item.description: Dear Parents and Guardians, Warm greetings from the Administration of Bright Sparks Junior School. As we approach the blessed occasion of Eid Al-Adha, I take this opportunity on…
item.content:encoded:
Dear Parents and Guardians,

Warm greetings from the Administration of Bright Sparks Junior School.

As we approach the blessed occasion of Eid Al-Adha, I take this opportunity on behalf of the management, teaching, and non-teaching staff to extend our warmest wishes to you and your families.

Eid Al-Adha is a profound reminder of the values of devotion, obedience, and selflessness. As a school community, we greatly appreciate the sacrifices you make daily to ensure our children receive the best foundation for their future.

May this holy season bring immense blessings, peace, and joy to your homes. Let us use this time to reflect on unity, kindness, and charity within our community.

Please Note:

  • School will break for the Eid holiday to allow our families to celebrate together.
  • We kindly remind you to ensure our learners remain safe and find some time to engage in light revision during the break.

We wish you all a safe, peaceful, and wonderful Eid Al-Adha celebration!

Eid Mubarak!

Warm regards,

Muneeb Ali Wanyeni

Head Teacher

Bright Sparks Junior School, Seguku Katale

item.title: Welcome Back to School for Term II 2026!
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: The start of a new term brings exciting opportunities for learning and growth.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Parents and Guardians,

At Bright Sparks, we believe that learning is an adventure. We are committed to walking with every child, encouraging them to embrace challenges, learn from mistakes, and grow into confident, capable young people.

Thank you for trusting us with your children's education and growth. We look forward to partnering with you this term to ensure a smooth, productive, and rewarding experience for every learner.

item.title: Educational Tours for P.1–P.7 — July 2026
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: Educational tours are planned for all classes from July 14–21, 2026. Destinations include the Airport & Zoo, Source of the Nile, and Murchison Falls.
item.content:encoded:
Exciting educational tours are planned for all classes from July 14–21, 2026. This is a highlight of the Term II calendar and a wonderful learning experience for every pupil.

Tour destinations by class:

  • P.1 – P.2: Entebbe Airport & Uganda Wildlife Conservation Centre (Zoo)
  • P.3 – P.4: Source of the Nile, Jinja
  • P.5 – P.7: Murchison Falls National Park
  • Kindergarten: Local educational site (details to follow)

Tour fees are separate from term fees. Please see our Fees Structure page or contact the school office for details. Consent forms and payment schedules will be distributed during the first weeks of term.

item.title: Cookery & Baking Club Prepares for Academic Day Exhibition
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: Our young chefs in the Cookery & Baking Club have been busy preparing for the Academic Day & Club Exhibitions scheduled for July 11, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The Bright Sparks Cookery & Baking Club has been working hard in preparation for the Academic Day & Club Exhibitions on July 11, 2026.

Under the guidance of their club teacher, pupils have been mastering recipes ranging from cakes and biscuits to savoury dishes. The club meets bi-weekly each term and has grown into one of the most popular co-curricular activities at the school.

Parents, guardians, and the wider school community are warmly invited to attend Academic Day and see the pupils' creations firsthand. More details on timing and venue will be shared closer to the date.

item.title: Football Team Wins Against St. James Junior School
item.dc:creator: Bright Sparks Junior School
item.description: Our football team emerged victorious in a thrilling match against St. James Junior School, greatly boosting school spirit and pride across the campus.
item.content:encoded:
In an exciting inter-school football fixture held during Term I 2026, the Bright Sparks Junior School football team emerged victorious against St. James Junior School.

The match, played at our school grounds, saw our pupils demonstrate excellent teamwork, discipline, and sportsmanship throughout. The final score drew loud celebrations from pupils, staff, and parents who attended.

Head Teacher Muneeb Ali Wanyeni congratulated the team: "This win is a reflection of the hard work, dedication, and team spirit our pupils bring every day — both on and off the pitch."

The school continues to encourage participation in sports as part of its holistic education approach.
